segments.title: Chương 12: 0012 [Tiểu thư hát tuồng]
segments.content:
There was gym class in the afternoon.

Today was exceptionally rare; the gym teacher was brimming with energy, and class hadn't been canceled due to some sudden illness.

The whole class was thrilled, forming small groups of threes and fives as they walked and laughed lightheartedly toward the large sports field.

At a time like this, there were hardly any bookworms still thinking about their studies.

Top students were top students because they knew when to study and when to play, managing to arrange their time efficiently and reasonably.

A few people had also gathered around Chen Guiliang: his roommates Xie Yang, Yang Hao, and Xu Haibo, as well as Guan Zhiqiang, one of the "Three Phantasmal Gods."

"Who was that girl who came looking for you at noon?" Xie Yang asked curiously.

Chen Guiliang said, "A first-year underclassman."

Xie Yang said with envy, "Not bad. When she was leaving, she passed by my desk. I got a good look; she's actually very pretty. Right, what's her name? Which first-year class is she in?"

"Don't know," Chen Guiliang said.

*Thump, thump, thump, thump…*

Li Jun was listening to music on his MP3 player, dribbling a basketball as he gradually caught up from behind.

Although the guy was obnoxious, he was on the school basketball team after all. He was good at basketball, so whenever it was gym class, there were always a few students who liked to play ball who would flock around him and play together.

"Damn it, Zheng Feng, you ditch your friends for a girl!"

One of the students playing basketball over there yelled at Zheng Feng, "Stop being a damn follower and come play basketball with us."

Zheng Feng's face flushed with embarrassment. He quickly ditched Bian Guanyue and ran over.

Without the lackey, Bian Guanyue instantly felt much more at ease.

She put on her earbuds and strolled leisurely, listening to music.

Wang Siyu and a few other girls she was close with came over to her, arm in arm. "Classmate Bian, what kind of music do you usually listen to? Do you listen to Jay Chou?"

"I do," Bian Guanyue said, taking off one earbud.

Although she acted extremely cold, she wasn't truly the type to just do whatever she wanted.

Take this moment for example. When someone spoke to her, she took off one earbud. One reason was to show basic respect to the other person, and the other was because she was afraid of missing what was said.

Wang Siyu said, "My favorite is 'East Wind Breaks.' Which Jay Chou song do you like?"

"'In the Name of the Father,'" Bian Guanyue answered.

"My favorite is 'Sunny Day.'"

"'Nunchucks' is obviously the coolest."

"'Love in BC,' 'Love in BC'!"

"…"

Several girls joined the discussion one after another. With Jay Chou as the topic, they chattered on and on.

In a flash, they arrived at the large sports field.

Class hadn't started yet, so all the basketball courts were taken. They'd have to wait a while for an opening.

Li Jun placed the basketball on the ground and pointed to a leaf on a tree, saying, "Bet you I can jump up and touch it?"

Naturally, no one believed him.

Li Jun immediately took off his jacket and, while slowly rolling up his sleeves, glanced at Bian Guanyue. To attract the girls' attention, he raised his voice and shouted, "Everyone watch, I'm going for it!"

Sure enough, a few girls looked over.

Li Jun took a few running steps and leaped up forcefully. Not only did he touch the leaf, but he also plucked it off. He said smugly, "Piece of cake. It's just a tiny bit higher than the rim. I can dunk with ease usually!"

"Wow!"

Many students, both boys and girls, let out cries of amazement.

Li Jun stood with his hands on his hips, his neck straight as he looked down on everyone, feeling like he was the absolute shit.

Xie Yang commented in a low voice, "Idiot."

Xu Haibo also said, "All brawn and no brains."

Chen Guiliang chuckled.

In a flash, the class bell rang, and the gym teacher blew his whistle at the edge of the field.

After taking attendance, the gym teacher said, "There's nothing much planned for today. After a one-thousand-meter slow run, you'll have free time. We'll gather for attendance again before class ends. You need to warm up before running, so follow me through a set of exercises."

During the warm-up, everyone's movements were loose and sloppy, as if being too serious would get them laughed at.

Only Chen Guiliang's form was the most standard. He felt that he really needed to work on his physique.

"Alright, warm-up's done. One-thousand-meter slow run. No slacking, I'm watching."

The whistle blew, and the run began.

Before they had even reached five hundred meters, the class had clearly separated into several distinct groups.

Chen Guiliang was in the middle group, neither at the front nor the back. But he still felt a bit weak. He needed to keep eating more meat to build himself up; this small frame of his hadn't yet recovered from long-term malnutrition.

Starting tomorrow, I'll wake up early to exercise and stick to running.

After the one-thousand-meter run, people were scattered across the field in disarray.

Some had even slacked off and taken a shortcut. The gym teacher pretended not to see, only saying to the students who were lying down from exhaustion, "Don't lie down or sit immediately after exercising. Everybody up, walk it off!"

Li Jun stood with one hand on his hip, pointing at the others with his other hand. "Haha, you guys are too weak. It's only a thousand meters and you're already done for."

A bunch of classmates shot him looks of disgust.

Chen Guiliang clutched his stomach, breathing heavily as he walked slowly. He had run pretty well for the first five hundred meters, and his sprinting bursts were especially explosive. But he was quite lacking in long-distance running. Halfway through, his stamina couldn't keep up. He still needed to supplement his nutrition and exercise more.

Bian Guanyue had also finished running by this point, her face not red and her breathing not labored. A thousand meters was a breeze for her.

"Old Bian, you're in pretty good shape," Chen Guiliang said, having caught his breath.

This form of address was a bit unexpected. Bian Guanyue asked doubtfully, "Are you calling me?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Yeah. If you don't like it, I can call you Xiao Bian from now on."

Bian Guanyue didn't answer him and put in her earbuds to listen to music.

Sigh, this one is really hard to deal with.

Chen Guiliang didn't even know what hobbies she had. If he asked, she wouldn't say, and beating around the bush was useless.

She was just very mysterious.

Extremely challenging. Chen Guiliang's interest grew immensely.

"Hero Chen, let's play some table tennis!" Xu Haibo shouted from a distance.

"Coming, coming!"

Chen Guiliang answered twice, then asked Bian Guanyue again, "Wanna play table tennis?"

Bian Guanyue shook her head. "No, thanks."

Chen Guiliang said no more and jogged towards the table tennis tables.

"A report from the disciplinary office, a report from the disciplinary office, Jay Chou from Year Three, Class Two, please come to the disciplinary office immediately…"

His roommate Li Yulin started singing while holding a racket. The battered guitar in their dorm room belonged to him, and he was also the one who got scared and ran off during his date by the man-made lake that night.

During his second year of high school, Chen Guiliang had even learned guitar from Li Yulin.

But his progress was limited; he only learned to play "Two Tigers" and "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star."

After Chen Guiliang left the field, Bian Guanyue turned down invitations from several other girls.

She circled the field by herself. Her MP3 player was on at some point, and Stefanie Sun's "Sky" played through her earbuds.

"My sky, why is it filled with wet tears."

"My sky, why is its face always gray."

"Drifting to the other side of the world, letting loneliness invade me again and again…"

On the east side of the field, students were playing table tennis.

On the west side, students were playing basketball.

In the center was the soccer field, where some students were playing soccer.

There were also many girls gathered and chatting, smiling in groups of threes and fives, talking about who knows what amusing things.

None of this seemed to have anything to do with Bian Guanyue.

It was as if she had been extracted from this world, empty and vast above, below, and all around.

Only a song and a single person remained.

Another pair of aces, another tragic love story. Can't we have something nice for a change?

In the blink of an eye, a week had passed since Chen Guiliang's rebirth.

Besides gradually getting closer to Bian Guanyue, he spent the rest of his time refamiliarizing himself with his high school textbooks.

English and math gave him the biggest headaches!

He had to go home to get his first and second-year textbooks and catch up, chapter by chapter.

The Mengya magazine publisher should have received his manuscript by now. But whether his article had been read was hard to say. After all, with over 400,000 submissions, it would take the organizers more than a month to review them all.

Friday, morning classes ended.

Bian Guanyue initiated the conversation. "Did you finish yesterday's geography worksheet?"

"I did," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue said, "There's a long-answer question I don't know how to do. Can I borrow yours to take a look?"

"Here." Chen Guiliang took the worksheet out of his desk drawer.

Bian Guanyue took the worksheet, folded it in half, and put it in her school bag.

Zheng Feng tried to curry favor. "I've finished my worksheet too."

Bian Guanyue pretended not to hear him, picked up her bag, and walked out.

Zheng Feng hurried after her.

One after the other, they walked to the bus stop to wait.

Many day students were waiting for the bus.

A moment later, before the bus had even come to a complete stop, Zheng Feng squeezed his way in like his life depended on it.

He pushed his way to the front with all his might and soon spotted two empty seats together. He ran over in a few steps, sat down with a thud, and used his bag to save the seat next to him.

"Bian Guanyue, there's a seat here!" Zheng Feng shouted, trying to take credit.

Bian Guanyue frowned slightly. She didn't like it when people did this. She would rather stand the whole way than owe someone a favor.

But if she refused, it would seem like she didn't consider Zheng Feng a friend.

Yes, although she was cold towards Zheng Feng, she already considered him a friend.

Chen Guiliang and Wang Siyu were her friends too.

Bian Guanyue walked over and sat down. Being so close, Zheng Feng grew tense and awkward. He was terrified of offending his goddess, so he scooted his bottom to the side, careful not to let his clothes even touch hers.

To Zheng Feng, time seemed to fly. In a flash, they arrived at Bian Guanyue's stop.

He got off the bus with her, planning to walk one stop home.

Zheng Feng stood foolishly by the roadside, watching as Bian Guanyue walked into a small alley.

This was part of the old city district.

The backstreets, in the strictest sense, still had perfectly preserved buildings from the late Qing and Republican eras. The government had plans to convert it into a tourist attraction.

Where Bian Guanyue lived was part of the backstreets in a broader sense, filled with old staff apartment buildings.

All the neighbors knew each other very well; there were no secrets.

Zheng Feng had indirectly asked his elders about it. He knew that Bian Guanyue's maternal grandparents were both retired workers from the cotton mill.

Bian Guanyue had an uncle who was currently a civil servant in the city. He had moved to the city with his wife and child.

As for Bian Guanyue's mother, she had remarried and moved to Pengcheng after her divorce.

Zheng Feng hadn't managed to find out any exact information about Bian Guanyue's father yet.

Seeing Bian Guanyue disappear around the corner, Zheng Feng quickly followed her again. He only turned back to go home after watching the goddess enter her building.

Bian Guanyue lived on the sixth floor.

Once she saw there was no one else in the stairwell, the usually aloof and cold Bian Guanyue seemed to suddenly become lively.

Her steps were light as she climbed the stairs, and she hummed a little tune, sometimes taking two or three steps at a time.

She put away her key and pushed the door open.

Her grandfather was in the kitchen, cooking.

Her grandmother was tending to the flowers and plants on the balcony. Hearing the door open, she said, "Guan Guan is back!"

"I'm back."

A brilliant smile bloomed on Bian Guanyue's face, making her look like a completely different person from how she was outside.

She tossed her school bag onto the sofa and walked over to the television to face the wall.

The wall was covered with old newspapers, and on them were many footprints.

Bian Guanyue suddenly lifted her left leg and stamped her foot on the newspaper on the wall, then pressed the upper half of her body forward.

As she stretched her leg, she regulated her breathing.

After a moment of preparation, Bian Guanyue began to sing from the Sichuan opera "The Story of the Red Plum":

"Red plums on the branch signal spring's delight, only to meet a gentleman standing on the painted bridge."

"I break off a fragrant branch for the young man, may you not fail the heart I secretly send today."

"As the wind passes, my sleeves flutter. How can I stop my heart from pounding, my soul from swaying…"

As she sang, Bian Guanyue's entire demeanor changed.

Her eyes, in particular, were captivating, enough to steal one's soul.

Traditional opera actors must practice the five methods: hand, eye, body, technique, and step.

A frown or a smile, sorrow or joy, could all be clearly expressed through the eyes alone.

If she used this kind of gaze at school, she could charm all the boys in her class into a stupor.

Her grandmother came back into the living room from the balcony and sat on the sofa to watch her granddaughter sing. The wrinkles on her face smoothed out, and she smiled silently, her mouth unable to close.

After a short while, Bian Guanyue switched to the other leg.

Suddenly, the sound of a key in the lock came from outside, and then the door was pushed open.

Bian Guanyue thought her uncle had returned from the city. She turned her head, and her expression instantly turned icy. "What are you doing here?"

The visitor was her mother, Guan Xiaolin, who had long since remarried and moved to Pengcheng.

Guan Xiaolin was carrying several large and small gift boxes. Seeing her daughter, she immediately smiled warmly. "I heard from your aunt that you transferred schools, so I came back especially to see you. Why didn't you continue studying in Rongcheng? The conditions there are so much better. What can you learn coming back to the county town?"

Bian Guanyue said nothing and went back to her bedroom, slamming the door shut with a "bang."
